title: Tensors, Shapes & Memory
description: Study tensor axes and shape contracts, broadcasting without accidental expansion, views, copies and contiguous storage, and dtype and device consistency. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Tensor axes and shape contracts
lessons.description: Trace [4, 10, 8] through a final-axis linear projection to 5 features. Record the output shape and each axis meaning.
lessons.conceptOverview: A tensor shape is an interface between layers. Write down what each axis means before reshaping: batch, sequence, channel, or feature. A linear layer transforms the last feature axis and keeps preceding axes. Shape-compatible operations can still be semantically wrong when axes are swapped.
lessons.whyItMatters: The projection changes the final feature dimension and preserves batch and sequence axes.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A batch of 16 examples with 8 features passing through a layer with 5 outputs has shape [16, 5]. Treating 16 as the feature count changes the model rather than only its layout.

sections.title: Practice & verification

keyTakeaways: The projection changes the final feature dimension and preserves batch and sequence axes.
commonMistakes: The projection always flattens all axes into one vector.

lessons.title: Broadcasting without accidental expansion
lessons.description: Write the intended prediction and target shapes for scalar regression. Explain which reshape prevents pairwise broadcasting.
lessons.conceptOverview: Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right. Dimensions are compatible when equal or when one is 1; missing leading dimensions behave as size 1. This can silently create a larger result than intended. Check the resulting shape before interpreting a loss or metric.
lessons.whyItMatters: Match target and prediction shapes so each prediction is compared with its own target.

lessons.title: Views, copies and contiguous storage
lessons.description: Compare a transpose, a reshape, and an explicit clone. Record shape, strides, and whether editing one object changes the source.
lessons.conceptOverview: A view can share storage with its source, so modifying it may affect the original. Transposing changes the stride interpretation and may produce non-contiguous storage. reshape may return a view or a copy; code should not assume which. Use explicit copies when isolation matters.
lessons.whyItMatters: Storage sharing and contiguity must be checked separately from tensor shape.

sections.title: Worked example
sections.content: A transposed matrix still refers to the same values in a different layout. A later flattening operation may require new contiguous storage rather than a cheap reinterpretation.

lessons.title: Dtype and device consistency
lessons.description: Create a device-and-dtype checklist for a classifier batch: inputs, labels, model parameters, and loss output.
lessons.conceptOverview: Tensor operations require compatible data types and devices. Integer labels often represent class indices, while activations and weights are floating point. Moving only the model to an accelerator leaves CPU inputs incompatible. Avoid unnecessary transfers inside tight loops because transfer and synchronization can dominate small computations.
lessons.whyItMatters: Move inputs and model consistently while keeping target dtype appropriate for the chosen loss.
